findings.summary: Product header bands on overview, list, about and settings screens hold only a title and a lead. They are stretched to fit a large trailing sticker, which leaves 80–140px of empty band colour, while the screen's search, pill tabs and filter field sit in the top bar or on paper below. The reference's header band (06) is compact and full: search, pill tabs and breadcrumb sit inside the colour field, with even padding. The same runs' detail screens, with breadcrumb and tabs inside the band, show how much better that reads. The spec causes this. It asks for a sticker at least as tall as the title block plus lead (200px on desktop), cropped by the trailing side only and never by a seam, and for the band to reserve room for it. The band then has to grow to the sticker. This was open in rc.3 and rc.4 review 1.
findings.promptFix: A header band is as tall as its content plus space.6–space.8 of padding above and below, never as tall as its sticker. Fill it with the screen's own controls, in this order: breadcrumb (when the screen has a parent), title, lead, then one row with the screen's search or filter field and its pill tabs or view filters. Any screen-level search, filter or tab row that would sit just under the band goes inside it instead. Fit the sticker to the band: as tall as the band's content height (never under size.stickerSm), at the trailing edge, and let the band's bottom seam crop it when it is taller. Never grow the band to fit the sticker. Below the last line of content, leave no more empty band colour than the band's own padding. A settings sub-screen's band carries no sticker.
findings.specRule: Header band. One sticker, at least as tall as the title block plus lead (`size.stickerBand` on desktop, never under `size.stickerSm`), centred at the trailing edge, cropped by that side only, never by a seam, at least 60% visible; the band reserves room so it never sits under a title, search or button.

findings.summary: Tables and plan cards put a pink notched flag in every row: budgets, small counts and every invoice. One sample also flags a percentage change. A column of six to eight flags becomes the loudest thing on the screen. The reference spends its hot colour on one or two accents and lets ink and paper carry a table. The spec's own wording leads agents to this.
findings.promptFix: In a table, a flag marks one figure for the whole table: its total, or the single row that matters. It never fills a column. Plain amounts are tabular ink text, and counts or percentages never get a flag. On a screen of cards, only the featured or current card's price is flagged.
findings.specRule: Item or plan cards (the price); one key amount cell per table row

findings.summary: Several states are underdrawn next to the reference's hairline controls. A hovered table row shows no change at all. The saved outcome on a form is a small pill, or a dot and a word, beside the buttons, and it nearly vanishes in dark mode. Buy-panel option chips mark the choice with a radio dot rather than 07's pink selected border. Disabled stepper buttons are grey-filled boxes. The empty cart's one action is a small default button rather than the screen's loudest piece. Several of these are carried over from rc.4.

On phones, pill and chip rows wrap and leave one item alone on a second line, or run off the edge mid-word: catalogue category pills, size chips and settings section links. The catalogue filter box spreads over tall, loose rows, and the store hero runs about 200px of empty band past its actions. The reference's phone screen (10) keeps one tight row and closes the band soon after its content.

In dark mode the drawn edges go soft. The black footer meets the black body with a faint rule or none, and so do some area bands. Dashed empty boxes and off switches nearly vanish on the raised fill. The 35% white hard shadow barely lifts dialogs and menus. The reference (11) closes every field and control with a crisp edge.

On desktop, form and detail bodies leave panels half-empty. Password fields stop at 40–55% of a full-width panel, and the project detail is a box nested inside a box that stops short of the content width. Reference 07 sets a description column beside the panel and draws one ink frame divided by rules, so nothing reads as dead space.

Sticker craft is uneven at the margins. Some hero stickers fall to about 100–130px, so the ring weighs less than 01's coins. On phones, lower hero stickers are cut about half away by the bottom seam. A few drawings fail as objects: a striped disc, a notched slab, a mug or basket whose depth sweeps sideways, and a billing sticker that copies the spec's example disc. The reference's stickers can each be named at a glance and share one depth direction.

Small departures from the ink-and-paper palette. In dark mode the header's trailing action is a dark-grey hairline cell rather than 11's solid pink full-height block. Article code blocks are grey-filled boxes, the search clear glyph is navy, and the post breadcrumb on phones wraps to three lines.

On phones, data tables cut a column mid-word at the frame with no sticky first column, scroll cue or ruled-list fallback, so row actions and statuses disappear. The dashboard's nav pill row runs past the right edge, with no menu button. The spec asks for the right behaviour, so these errors are the agents' own.

The account menu's last item sits flush against the panel's left edge, and in one sample it is underlined as a bare link. In one dark loading state, a control on a band turns into a dark-grey filled block.

notes: Review: 138/138 checklist items by 8 reviewer(s) and a lead reviewer (showcase/runs/felt-tip-market/0.1.0-rc.4/review-2).

The front pages read as the reference's own work: paper and lemon bands, a 96px headline, a black CTA beside a bordered field at one height, thick ink-outlined stickers cropped at the edges, the black current pill and the full-height header block, and a faithful dark inversion. The same family holds across all four apps.

The gap is on product screens. Header bands are padded to a 200px sticker the spec requires and stay empty, where 06's band is compact and full of controls. Pink flags fill whole table columns, which the spec's 'one per row' wording invites. States, phone rows and dark-mode edges are cruder than the reference's hairline controls. Fixing the two spec-caused rules should lift spacing and polish clearly.
